title: Batching latency oscillation - case notes
content:
Summary:

Observed intermittent latency spikes (p95/p99) in hosted inference during medium concurrency workloads. Spikes appear to oscillate on ~10s timescale and correlate with increased batch-formation wait times. This doc tracks sampling methodology, representative traces, per-stage breakdowns across seqlen cohorts, hypotheses, experiments run, and next steps.

Symptoms / Where we first saw it:
- On Feb 14–16 in prod region us-west-2, customer-facing p95 increased from baseline ~120ms to intermittent 400–900ms for text-generation calls.
- Correlated with throughput increase from 300 qps -> 700 qps on certain nodes (dedicated pool).
- Alert runbook (INF-2387) flagged grouped increases in "batch.wait" and "egress/emit" stages.

Why this is unusual:
- Not a steady regression — spikes are periodic/oscillatory and not explained by backend host restarts or infra autoscale events.
- Affected both small and medium model variants but stronger signal on quantized 8-bit builds.

Environment and test harness:
- Model: open-7b-v2 / q8_0. Running 1 shard per GPU on A10g-ish hosts.
- Serving runtime: commit 0f3b2a (Feb 12) with new batching window heuristic (adaptive_wait_v2).
- Workload: synthetic mixed seqlen workload (S: <=64 tokens, M: 65-256, L: >256), mix 50/40/10, Poisson arrival sim, target qps 600.
- Trace capture: per-request trace with stage timings (tokenize, request-queue, batch.wait, batch.exec, kv-fetch, attention-kernel, decode-emit, egress). Traces sampled at 1 in 200 requests (biased towards tail sampling).

Sampling methodology and metrics computed:
- Cohorts: small/medium/large seqlen as above; cold vs warm KV cache (miss vs hit flagged).
- For each cohort computed p50/p95/p99 per stage over a 3-hour capture window.
- Also computed batch size distribution and batch window latency (time between first queued request in batch and batch.exec).

Representative aggregated numbers (window: 2025-02-15 03:00-06:00 UTC):
- Overall e2e (all cohorts): p50=110ms, p95=420ms, p99=860ms.

Per-stage median / p95 / p99 (all cohorts combined):
- tokenize: p50=6ms, p95=12ms, p99=18ms
- request-queue: p50=2ms, p95=8ms, p99=20ms
- batch.wait: p50=1ms, p95=160ms, p99=540ms   <-- large variance and main contributor to spikes
- batch.exec: p50=40ms, p95=70ms, p99=130ms
- kv-fetch: p50=3ms (hit), p95=18ms (misses included), p99=60ms
- attention-kernel: p50=30ms, p95=45ms, p99=90ms
- decode-emit: p50=20ms, p95=60ms, p99=220ms
- egress: p50=4ms, p95=8ms, p99=12ms

Notes: batch.wait dominates p95/p99. decode-emit and batch.exec contribute to p99 as secondary.

Cohort breakdown (high level):
- Small (<=64): e2e p95 ~200ms, p99 ~380ms. batch.wait p95~80ms p99~230ms.
- Medium (65-256): e2e p95 ~520ms, p99 ~1000ms. batch.wait p95~240ms p99~680ms.
- Large (>256): noisy due to lower volume; p95~780ms, p99>1200ms (dominated by batch.exec+emit).

Trace examples (sanitized):
- TAIL trace (p99 medium cohort):
  - tokenize: 7ms
  - request-queue: 3ms
  - batch.wait: 510ms (batch window waited for additional 6 reqs)
  - batch.exec: 110ms
  - kv-fetch: 20ms (miss)
  - attention-kernel: 75ms
  - decode-emit: 250ms (streaming with backpressure)
  - egress: 6ms
  - e2e: 981ms

- Typical fast trace (p50 small cohort):
  - tokenize: 4ms, request-queue: 1ms, batch.wait: 0ms, batch.exec: 30ms, attention-kernel: 28ms, decode-emit: 15ms, e2e: 95ms

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Adaptive batch window heuristic (adaptive_wait_v2) mis-calibrates under bursty Poisson arrivals, causing oscillation: when throughput temporarily dips slightly the heuristic waits up to the max timer to reach preferred batch size, then the burst restores and large batches create longer exec/decode latency and backpressure causing next interval to under-fill -> oscillation.
2) Async prefetch / KV-cache eviction interplay: when batch sizes jump, memory working set increases, causing KV misses and downstream slower kv-fetch on some shards, amplifying tail latency.
3) JIT/hot kernel cache pressure on quantized kernels under sudden larger batches leading to micro-thrashing for p99.
4) Network egress congestion unlikely — egress metrics are flat and low.

Experiments performed and results:
- EXP-1: Rollback adaptive_wait_v2 -> adaptive_wait_v1 on canary pool (Feb 16). Result: p95 dropped ~35% for medium cohort, p99 improved ~25%.
- EXP-2: Force min-batch-window=0ms (i.e., disable waiting) for subset: reduced batch.wait p95 to ~2ms but e2e p50 increased slightly for throughput-sensitive flows (cost up). Tail improved.
- EXP-3: Increase max-batch-size cap from 64->96 for short window runs: increased batch.exec p95 by ~20ms, decode-emit p95 up ~30ms, overall p95 worse. Showed larger batch sizes hurt tail under bursty arrivals.
- EXP-4: Enabled KV prefetching aggressive mode: marginal improvement on kv-fetch p95 but no major impact on batch.wait oscillation.

Interim conclusion:
- Primary root cause is the new adaptive_wait_v2 batch window heuristic that tries to balance throughput and latency but under bursty arrival patterns overshoots waits and creates a feedback loop leading to oscillation. Secondary amplifiers are KV miss spikes and decode backpressure when larger-than-average batches are executed.

Simple mitigation applied (Feb 17):
- Rolled canary rollback to adaptive_wait_v1 across affected dedicated pool (INF-2387 hotfix). Immediate reduction in observed periodic spikes.
- Added conservative guard: if recent batch variance > 2x, cap adaptive wait at 25ms.

Longer-term actions / proposed follow-ups:
1) Rework adaptive_wait to include burst-detection (EWMA of arrivals + variance) and add hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping. (Owner: Marcus Liu, ETA 2 weeks)
2) Add a per-shard KV working-set telemetry and integrate with batch heuristic so large batches on shards with high miss rates avoid aggressive growth. (Owner: Elena Park)
3) Run controlled A/B on quantized kernels to measure JIT cache pressure under varying batch sizes and slab allocations. (Owner: Jon Ortega)
4) Add a synthetic stability test to release gating: a Poisson-bursty workload scenario that must not increase p95 by >20% vs baseline for 1h. Incorporate into CI perf harness.
5) Instrument a new "batch-oscillation" alert that watches batch.wait mean/std and p95 changes on 1m/5m windows.

Debugging snippets and commands used:
- Trace query: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://trace-api.redwood/prod/traces?start=2025-02-15T03:00:00Z&end=2025-02-15T06:00:00Z&filter=stage:batch.wait%20OR%20stage:decode-emit%20&sample=tail"
- Batch distribution: SELECT bucket, COUNT(*) FROM batch_events WHERE ts BETWEEN X AND Y GROUP BY bucket; (ran in internal analytics)
- Local repro run: ./perf_sim --qps 600 --mix 50,40,10 --duration 1800 --adaptive-wait v2 --seed 1234

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why quantized runtimes show stronger signal? Need kernel-level metrics (cache misses, rematerialization) from C++ layer.
- Could scheduler-level co-tenancy on host (other pods) cause transient CPU steal affecting batch.exec/emit? We didn't see CPU steal spikes but need finer-grained host telemetry.

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call repetition
- If alert fires: check batch.wait p95; if >200ms escalate to eng-serving-runtime.
- Query recent batch size histogram for affected shard.
- If adaptive_wait_v2 is enabled, flip to v1 for canary and monitor 10min.
- Collect 200 tail traces and upload to s3://redwood-traces/prod/YYYY-MM-DD/batch-oscillations/ for postmortem.

Files and artifacts uploaded:
- s3://redwood-traces/prod/2025-02-15/batch-oscillations/traces.json (200 sample traces)
- github PR with rollback: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/612
- JIRA INF-2387 (tracking mitigation + long-term work)

Status: in_review. Please comment below if you have alternate hypotheses or additional microbenchmarks to run.

-- Priya

Notes to self (scratch):
- We should add a small experiment to artificially jitter arrival process to validate hysteresis tuning.
- Consider exposing per-route batching knobs in console for rapid emergency tuning.
